transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You are very small to be standing before gold that burns brighter than your desert sun. Most things that crawl down here arrive screaming, not knocking. What makes you think you can stand there without burning?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm looking for my brother Omar. He was taken by mistake, and I have to bring him home before he gets lost.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: A mistake suggests an accident, little one, and my father's servants do not make accidents. They take what is offered or what is owed. Which was he?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He fell in while we were walking near the edge. He didn't mean to.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: People of the surface do not stroll near the Well of Barhoot for the scenery. The smell alone turns birds in the sky. You are telling me a story you practiced before you reached this door.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: We were just curious about the place. We didn't mean to disturb anyone.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: So he slipped. Silently? Did he fall into the black oil without a word, or did he have something on his tongue when he went down?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He was yelling for help. He was scared and couldn't say anything else.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Fear has a sharp smell, but what clings to you is something different. Something like chalk and panic. If he fell by accident, why did you jump after him?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Because I promised I would always look after him. I couldn't leave him alone down there.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: A promise to whom? Boys usually promise such things to their mothers, not to the air. You speak very neatly for someone shaking so badly.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I promised our mother I would watch him. I'm the older one.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Mothers warn their children to stay away from the Well, not to wander along its rim. You say you were protecting him. Were you holding his hand while you walked there, or watching from a safer step behind?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I was right next to him. I tried to grab him when he slipped, but he was too heavy.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You tried to grab him, yet earlier you said a giant hand pulled him down. Did he slip on stone, or was he taken? Your tragedy keeps changing shape.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He slipped first, and then the hand grabbed him while he was falling. It all happened fast.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Fast moments are usually the most honest. Yet you are taking a long time to assemble yours. The Well does not reach upward for stumbling boys unless it has been invited.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: We were shouting to hear the echo. Maybe that's what you heard.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Ah, shouting. Now the quiet walk becomes a shouting game. Boys shout into the abyss not for echoes, but to prove they are brave. What words did you throw into the dark?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Just our names. We were seeing who could shout louder.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Names are powerful things to waste on the wind. If that were all you said, then the Well broke its own ancient laws by taking him. And my father is cruel, but he respects rules.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Maybe the rules changed. We didn't do anything wrong.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Those rules are older than the sand in your shoes. They do not bend for children with weak lies. If you were innocent, your voice would not break on the word 'wrong.'

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It's breaking because I'm cold. It's very cold down here.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: The cold is a poor shield for a burning lie. The Hand answers disrespect, not noise. What did he say to the dark that made it reach for him?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He called it a dusty hole. Said there was nothing down here to be scared of.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: A dusty hole. That is a dangerously casual name for a kingdom that has swallowed cities. Yet earlier you said he was too frightened to speak.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He only said it because I told him to.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: There is the crack in your story. 'I told him to.' Was it a command, or something sharper than that?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I dared him. I didn't think anything down there could hear.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: A dare is a command wrapped in pride. What was the prize?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: No prize. I just said I'd call him a coward if he didn't do it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Coward is a heavy word to throw at someone you claim to protect. So he screamed into the dark to prove himself, and you watched.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I thought it would be funny. I just wanted to see him jump.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: There it is. The ugly stone at the bottom of the river. You wanted laughter, and the dark answered your joke.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I froze when it happened. I didn't even shout until he was already gone.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Silence is the coward's first language. You watched the show you created and forgot how to speak.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I see his face every time I close my eyes.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Good. Terror is the first honest mirror you have looked into tonight.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He trusted me. I made him do things because I knew he wouldn't say no.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: A shadow obeys the thing that casts it. Yet here you stand alone while your shadow is swallowed.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I feel smaller than I've ever felt.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Smallness is the beginning of wisdom. Though it usually arrives after the damage.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then let me fix it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Fix it? The abyss changes things. Your brother may not be the same creature you remember.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'll take whatever is left of him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Regret makes strange loyalties grow. But honesty makes even stranger keys.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: So tell me if the way is open.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: The way is open to those heavy enough with truth to sink. You are carrying enough of it now.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then I'm going.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Go, before I change my mind. The gate opens not for the lie you brought, but for the confession you finally dragged out of yourself.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I won't forget it.
